doc.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024

title: Playing the melody and discovering it after years of accompanying herself
summary: She discusses playing melody for passers-by, and realizes after two years of solo piano that she never played the melodies, now exploring them in new keys.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Do you have a sense of, especially on this type of gig you’re doing now, that people are going to enjoy what you play more if you make the melody predominant, like they’re used to hearing it sung? And the reason I ask that is I’ve heard some piano players who will take a song like “Spanish Eyes,” which has a certain groove to it, and they’ll just like be so — first rubato and then florid and all this stuff until it doesn’t even matter that the song is “Spanish Eyes”?

Understand. I understand what you’re saying. In my case in this particular venue, where people are just walking in and out and sometimes there’s hardly anybody there, I could do, you know, fifty choruses of what I think is “Spanish Eyes” but no one else would recognize it. And sometimes it probably is just as well because it just sounds nice and it’s elevator music, you know, it really is. But in general I definitely try — and actually here is another, well secret or a confession, most of my performances through the years is singing along with my playing, maybe playing solos here and there which I would enjoy, but it’s still the singing. So this is, now it’s been over two years of just piano, and I really didn’t give it that much thought when I took the job and started playing. And I started © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

playing all these songs that I know and then suddenly every once in a while you know it’s like my fingers are like going to a note pattern and my fingers are just going to wrong notes and I’m realizing, Daryl, you never played the melody in all these years if you’re accompanying yourself. So number one give yourself a break. Don’t feel bad about it because it’s amazing that you can do it. Actually I do amaze myself and then I play it in all different keys.
And mostly my fingers are doing more for me than any other part of my body right now.
Oh that’s a good statement. That’s right. Your fingers almost sense okay I know this has got to go up the scale or there’s this little leap here.

You just go there. I don’t know how it happens I swear to you I don’t know. It’s divine intervention, but it has then made me aware of that so I’m using this to play all of these and try them in different keys and all of a sudden realizing well I always played it in that key because my vocal range, it suited that — but oh listen to how beautiful the melody sounds in this register, because I’m a painter. So I’m having a good time, and it’s — and you know I’m at this [gulp] age but I’m not dead and I’m still learning and loving it.
